summary: Sporting News live tracker of news, rumors, signings and trades from the 2023 MLB Winter Meetings in Nashville (Dec. 3-6). The biggest developments were the Yankees' reported trade for Juan Soto, the Diamondbacks landing Eduardo Rodriguez, and the Orioles signing Craig Kimbrel, while the market waited on Shohei Ohtani's decision. The tracker also covers Yoshinobu Yamamoto's pursuit, trade candidates like Corbin Burnes and Dylan Cease, and many smaller deals.
one_line: Day-by-day tracker of 2023 MLB Winter Meetings moves, including the Juan Soto trade to the Yankees and the ongoing Shohei Ohtani sweepstakes.
key_facts: The 2023 MLB Winter Meetings ran Sunday, Dec. 3 through Wednesday, Dec. 6 in Nashville.
The Padres reportedly sent Juan Soto to the Yankees for four pitchers and catcher Kyle Higashioka, per the New York Post's Joel Sherman; Trent Grisham was also likely to go to New York.
Jon Morosi reported Michael King and Drew Thorpe would headline San Diego's return for Soto, and that Alex Verdugo would not be in the package.
Eduardo Rodriguez reportedly agreed to a four-year deal with Arizona worth around $20 million per year, pending a physical; he had a 3.30 ERA over 152.2 innings with the Tigers.
The Orioles signed Craig Kimbrel to a one-year, $13 million deal with a $1 million buyout for 2025 and a $13 million club option; he has 417 career saves, eighth all-time.
The Yankees acquired Alex Verdugo from the Red Sox for RHP Richard Fitts, RHP Greg Weissert and RHP Nicholas Judice, only the seventh Red Sox-Yankees deal in 50 years.
Ohtani had reportedly received several offers above $500 million, and his deal could reach $600 million, the largest guaranteed contract in North American sports history.

Ohtani's finalists were reported as the Dodgers, Blue Jays, Angels and Giants, with the Cubs' optimism fading; he reportedly met the Blue Jays in Florida on Monday, Dec. 4, and the Dodgers for 2-3 hours.
Jon Morosi reported Ohtani was expected to decide before the end of the weekend following the meetings.

The Braves acquired Jarred Kelenic, Marco Gonzales and Evan White from the Mariners for Cole Phillips and Jackson Kowar; Gonzales was then re-routed to Pittsburgh for cash and a player to be named later.
Victor Caratini agreed to a two-year, $12 million deal with the Astros to back up Yainer Diaz.
Wade Miley returned to the Brewers on a one-year deal with a $7 million base salary and a $12 million mutual option for 2025.
Korean outfielder Jung Hoo Lee, 25, was posted by the Kiwoom Heroes, starting a 30-day negotiating window on Tuesday at 8 a.m. ET.
Yoshinobu Yamamoto was expected to meet the Yankees on Monday after already meeting Mets owner Steve Cohen in Japan; the Giants might have an edge, per Susan Slusser.
